page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on KVM hypervisor architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs provisioned from 16 physical AMD EPYC 9T24 cores running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Hardware instruction set extensions include AVX-512, VNNI, BF16, AES, and VAES for accelerated cryptographic and vector processing. This configuration includes no local instance storage and relies on external block storage, while network throughput is backed by a 10 Gbps baseline interface.

Performance metrics highlight strong single-core efficiency, supported by a Geekbench single-core score of 2002.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3072.08. Synthetic evaluation demonstrates high cryptographic throughput, evidenced by a PassMark CPU encryption score of 38480.15. Geekbench multi-core testing scored 16430.0 alongside strong performance in text and image processing tasks. Multi-core stress-ng performance (49187.43) and static web serving throughput (29.93 GB/sec) remain in average benchmark ranges, reflecting trade-offs under high sustained multi-threaded saturation.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio renders this instance cost-efficient for compute-heavy applications that do not require large memory capacity per core. Omitting bundled local storage minimizes baseline hardware overhead, allowing resource allocation to focus on processor capacity and network connectivity. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.8xlarge is best suited for compute-intensive workloads such as batch processing, code compilation, cryptographic services, web server clusters, and microservice infrastructure.
